title.narrative: Starting a sustainable, cooperative and fully circular coffee farm in Mubende district, Uganda

description.narrative: Uganda is internationally considered the birthing place of Robusta coffee. Coffee that is produced in Uganda often has limited added value by the farmers. Dutch social enterprise the Brand Development Group is investing in setting up a model coffee farm based on principles of the “Circular Economy” of 80 acres in Mubende Uganda. This “Brand Coffee Farm Uganda” is growing robusta coffee in a different way to create an improved value addition. Furthermore the farm will support/train local small holder farmers’ activities to improve their livelihoods. In order to have a positive impact early on and to improve existing production methods, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) supports this project. The project includes support to set-up a circular coffee farm using sustainable production methods, to prepare for International certification and exports and to transfer knowledge regarding circular and sustainable production methods, post-harvest handling and good agricultural practices to farmers in the region. The project is ongoing and already supports 22 direct jobs, 10 indirect jobs and an 40 seasonal workers during harvest seasons. It also contributes to knowledge transfer by training +4,000 and growing smallholder coffee farmers and farmers of other crops on sustainable methods, using organic techniques such as beekeeping and planting cash crops (e.g. avocado-, mango-, cashew trees) for shadow, creating additional income for farmers. To create more impact, Brand Coffee Farm Uganda has founded the Large Scale Coffee Farmers Association , with 21 members who will implement and share Brand Coffee Farm’s knowledge and experience with small holders. Each large coffee farm reaches 5,000 farmers and can improve the livelihoods of 10,000 families through this farming model. A youth employment program, to provide services to these farmers, is also being set-up. Furthermore, hundreds of individual farmers from the region, mostly female, are using the lands of Brand Coffee Farm to produce their own crops, creating an increased livelihood in the community. Certification of the coffee will take place in 2021 and, further investments in land, washing stations are prepared which create an additional 20 jobs.
